Marriage ends in seven days after bride reveals prior relationship, Indore family court grants divorce

An Indore Family Court reportedly dissolved a marriage within seven days after the bride disclosed soon after the wedding that she had been in a relationship with another person and had entered the marriage under family pressure.

According to the report, both sides agreed that the marriage could not continue and approached the Family Court for divorce. The court found no realistic possibility of reconciliation and decided not to prolong the dispute through extended proceedings.

The matter was treated as unusual because matrimonial cases ordinarily involve counselling, hearings and procedural waiting periods. In this case, however, the court reportedly concluded that continuing the marriage on paper would serve no useful purpose.

Accordingly, the marriage was dissolved within seven days, allowing both parties to separate without prolonged litigation.
comment: Such cases also highlight the importance of informed consent in marriage. Early transparency can prevent years of emotional distress and complex matrimonial litigation later.
